evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: The scope and behavior are concrete and specific (fields and outcome), so a reasonable implementation estimate can be made.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Clearly scoped (generate/send URL and access), so estimatable without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Specific UI action and artifact described; scope is small and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Clear display requirement (list of session items); implementable and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Concrete interaction (select item) and outcome; scope is small enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Well-scoped CRUD operation; can be estimated without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: A specific edit capability; sufficiently specified for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specific delete operation; small and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Behavior is concrete (reveal estimates immediately even if not all submitted); implementation scope is clear.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Specific calculation and UI behavior; estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Clear trigger and result; small, implementable feature that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Concrete UI action (enter agreed estimate) with clear outcome; estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Behavior is specific (re-estimate earlier story); scope is narrow enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Import functionality is a common, bounded feature; format details could be clarified but the story is estimateable at feature level.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specific input mechanism with clear scope; can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing/searching historical games is a well-bounded feature; estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Displaying stored transcript is concrete and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specific export format and artifact; scope clear for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Clear export requirement with concrete format; estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Well-scoped delete operation; can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Fields are enumerated and behavior is standard account creation; estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Standard authentication behavior; clear and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Typical update-account functionality; scope is small and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Specific, bounded operation with clear outcome; can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Clear technical requirement (timezone conversion/display); estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Standard password reset/reminder flow; sufficiently specified for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Enumerated choices make the feature concrete and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Numeric limit defines scope; straightforward to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Clear join flow and inputs; estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Simple display requirement with explicit purpose; can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Clear list-display functionality; scoped and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Concrete UI indication requirement; implementable and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Well-defined trigger and behavior; scope is clear for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Specific timing condition for edits; small, estimateable feature.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Requirement to display historical estimates is concrete enough to estimate (UI + data retrieval), even if exact history window can be refined later.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Clear mapping of estimator to estimate in current round; implementable and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specific timer length and visibility; well-bounded and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Clear trigger and behavior for the timer; can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Browsing historical rounds is a defined UI/data feature; estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Deterministic card ordering is specific and implementable; estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Clearly defined condition for allowing changes; scope is small and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Specific UI element and placement; implementable and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a concrete target (specific standards exist); estimatable as a QA/implementation task.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Creating a definitions list is a bounded documentation task and can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: 'Queries run as fast as possible' and which queries need indexing are unspecified, making scope and effort unclear and hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Browsers and versions are explicitly listed, so compatibility effort is well-scoped and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: The phrase 'where possible' and lack of which accessibility guidelines or success criteria to target leaves scope underspecified and hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: 'Respond quickly' is vague without performance targets or measurable criteria, making implementation effort difficult to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a concrete technical requirement (character encoding, input/display); scope is estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Although subjective, creating a consistent URL scheme is a bounded design/implementation task that can be estimated at feature level.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Designing friendly error pages is a concrete UI/content task; effort is bounded and estimateable.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Anonymization requirements are underspecified (which fields, anonymization standard), making the work and complexity hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: 'Some metrics' is vague (which metrics, aggregation, retention), so scope is too unspecified to estimate implementation effort.
